newsitem.title: UK: Gold prices sink to new 3-3/4 year low.
newsitem.headline: Gold prices sink to new 3-3/4 year low.

text.p: Gold prices fell to their lowest levels since the middle of April 1993 as a fresh surge in the value of the U.S. dollar provoked dumping of the precious metal, dealers said.
Gold fixed at $336.90 per ounce, down from $339.40 on Tuesday, to record its lowest London fixing since April 13, 1993.
The rush by the dollar to regain a 34-month high against the mark and close to a four-year peak against the yen began on Tuesday afternoon.
But by mid-morning Wednesday statements by Bundesbank officials that the dollar had corrected and should not rise further, helped rein the U.S. currency back under 1.68 marks.
The respite for gold was marginal and a lift off the floor of about $336.50 bid was not seen to be necessarily sustainable.
"There are a few bids coming in but every morning there is more selling. It is unrelenting at the moment," one dealer said.

Some dealers said sales came from long term investors finally deciding that gold was not going to get back to its high levels of the early 1980s, with some seeing a chance to bale out - as the value of dollar-denominated gold in their own currencies is propped up by the dollar's strength.
"The bank vaults are getting emptier every day," one dealer based in continental Europe said.
Others hinted at central bank selling but most agreed that gold producers were responsible for at least some of the pressure.
The fall in the gold's value which has accelerated since the beginning of the year after drifting lower most of 1996, has increased pressure on mine profit margins.
"It looks like producer selling for the short term," a dealer said, pointing to the rise in gold's short term borrowing rates.
The producers could be borrowing from the central banks to sell to the maret or roll-over contracts as they come due.
Dealers were unsure how much further the market could fall possibly to the March 30, 1993 low of $332.20.
Silver prices were also sharply lower at $4.81/$4.83 down 11 cents after positions had been unwound in New York on Tuesday.
Platinum was $1.75 lower at $352.75/$353.75 but palladium retained its recent firmness at $135.25/$135.25, up $1.50.
Tightness caused by the delay in setting Russia-Japan 1997 export contracts plus speculative buying supported the market.
